sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mail-Order Retail with Cash on Delivery Settlement

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law, Samoan customary law, and territorial statute law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: WTO (Samoa has been a member since 10 May 2012)
PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus, in force 13 December 2020)
Samoa–Germany Bilateral Investment Treaty (1973, inherited from pre-independence practice; narrow application)
Automatic exchange of financial account information under the US Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (IGA) and OECD Common Reporting Standard

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 2011 (Samoa), Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended), Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Regulations 2020, Financial Intelligence Unit Directive on Enhanced Due Diligence, and the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) AML/CFT Guidelines for International Companies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of constitutional document (Memorandum and Articles of Association) of any parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and competent consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy and proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner, director, and shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the applicant's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or Hague Apostille where the issuing state is an Apostille Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the applicant entity or ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or financial institution in the applicant's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or Apostille, plus direct verification to issuer where required by the Samoan registered agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified corporate registration certificate and certificate of incumbency for any legal entity shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of companies or accredited corporate services provider in the origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or Apostille depending on origin jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/CFT compliance questionnaire and source-of-wealth declaration for the beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Samoan registered agent and the applicant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus consular legalization if executed outside Samoa

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, signatories, and material counterparties against the United Nations consolidated sanctions list, OFAC specially designated nationals list, Samoan consolidated sanctions list, EU and UK sanctions lists, and INTERPOL alerts. Enhanced due diligence is required for any cash-on-delivery remittance corridor involving emerging markets; automated screening and risk scoring must be updated at least every 24 hours and cleared records must be retained for at least five years after incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – Online International Companies Registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin script; names in Chinese or other non-Latin scripts are accepted only if submitted with a precise official English/Samoan transliteration, and the registered Latin-script name is controlling for all legal filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of a name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the SIFA Registrar accompanied by legal submissions, a corrected name proposal, and the applicable appeal fee. The Registrar must issue a determination within 30 business days. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may file a judicial review application in the Supreme Court of Samoa under the International Companies Act 2011 within 21 days of the refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable. Samoa requires a physical registered office maintained by a licensed registered agent. For an e-commerce cash-on-delivery business, remote administrative operations are permissible provided the registered agent's physical address in Apia is designated and the company maintains no local trading activity that would create a taxable presence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium–low (approximately 8% annual likelihood for a standard international company; increases to 20% where cash-on-delivery settlement and emerging-market counterparties trigger enhanced AML/CFT scrutiny).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for Samoa international companies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office provision and mail forwarding (annual)
UBO register preparation, AML/CFT file, PEP and sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance officer of the registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and FIU circulars

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and consular legalization of passport and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and Samoan consular services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular tariff and notary fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Courier delivery of legalized documents and authenticated records
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: International courier rate for Apia, Samoa

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (No. 17 of 1987) as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2017, Part II (Incorporation and Powers), Part III (Memorandum and Articles), Part V (Directors and Officers); read with the International Companies Regulations 1988 and the SIFA AML/CFT Beneficial Ownership Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, commercial registry functions administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) and the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC-1 Application for Registration of an International Company, submitted with the executed Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no capital escrow or bank deposit requirement; the Memorandum must state an authorised share capital, which may be denominated in any currency, and shares may be par value, no par value, issued or partly paid.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Memorandum and Articles of Association tabled at this meeting are approved and adopted without amendment. (2) [Registered Agent], a licensed agent under the International Companies Act 1987, is appointed first registered agent of the Company. (3) The registered office of the Company is established at the agent's registered address in Apia, Samoa. (4) [Name] and [Name] are appointed first directors; [Name] is appointed Chairperson and [Name] is appointed Company Secretary. (5) The directors are authorised to open domestic and international bank and payment accounts, using Airwallex and local logistics remittance rails, and to execute every document required to give full effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage Licensed Registered Agent and Reserve Company Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed registered agent acting through the Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a SIFA-licensed agent to submit a name reservation request and conduct an AML preliminary screen. The proposed name must end with 'International Company' or the abbreviation 'IC', must not conflict with an existing Samoa domestic or international company, and must not contain restricted words such as Bank, Trust, Insurance or Co-operative unless specific consent is obtained. The agent lodges the name reservation with the Registry and pays the applicable reservation fee.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and three alternates
Passport copies and proof of address of subscriber and beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusing similarity, obtain written reasons from the Registrar and file a statutory declaration of distinctiveness; any adverse determination may be appealed to the Chief Executive Officer of MCIL within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed registered agent and notary public in Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles on the statutory form. The objects clause must include full commercial powers covering mail-order and electronic retail (ISIC 4791), cash-on-delivery settlement, logistics management, payment facilitation and ancillary treasury functions. Each subscriber executes the Memorandum before a notary or attesting witness; the registered agent executes its consent to act. The authorised share capital is stated in the Memorandum.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as registered agent
Subscriber KYC files and notarised identification copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective pages may be substituted and re-executed before filing; if already lodged, the Registrar may accept amended documents on requisition without court application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodge Incorporation Application and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies (SIFA / MCIL Commercial Registry), Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form IC-1 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles, the registered agent's consent, and a statutory declaration of compliance. Pay the government registration fee of US$350 per the current SIFA fee schedule. The Registrar reviews the application for compliance, registers the company, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation of an International Company, which is conclusive evidence of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a requisition, cure the deficiency within 30 days by filing the requested correction; late cure attracts a minor late-filing fee. Refusal of registration is appealable to the Minister within 21 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitute Corporate Governance and Establish Bank and Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or adopt a written resolution approving the company's governance. Appoint first directors, Chairperson and Company Secretary, adopt the registered office and corporate seal, approve share allotments and issue share certificates, and open bank and payment processor accounts, including Airwallex and local logistics remittance providers, after completing the institution's AML due diligence.
required_dossiers: Register of shareholders and return of allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If particulars of directors are rejected by the agent's compliance team, file corrected identity documents within 7 days; no material penalty is imposed where the correction is completed before the next regulatory filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Beneficial Ownership Filings and Tax-Exempt Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent, SIFA, and Ministry of Revenue (tax exemption confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial ownership register with the registered agent in line with the SIFA AML/CFT Rules; apply for the standard tax exemption confirmation letter recognising the International Company's exemption from Samoan income tax and stamp duty; obtain a Certificate of Good Standing. For cash-on-delivery payment flows, submit the payment rails' compliance questionnaires to satisfy external AML reviews.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late beneficial ownership filings are excusable by voluntary disclosure with a written explanation; deliberate non-compliance may be compounded, so cure the default immediately upon notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing board. Samoa does not require a manufacturing or operational permit for remote mail-order retail under ISIC 4791; domestic business registration may be required only if a physical retail counter is opened.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable. If the company later adds physical warehousing or fulfilment, a Business Activity Permit from the Samoa Commerce Industry Desk and a warehouse occupancy certificate would be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Samoa Environmental Protection Agency, Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 3. Pure trading and e-commerce operations generate no EIA report obligation; an Environmental Screening may be triggered only if warehousing exceeds 500 square metres or cold-storage expands to industrial scale.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC or combustion emissions are generated by ISIC 4791; general standards apply: solid waste disposal through approved municipal collection under the Waste Management Act 2010, and stormwater from any leased warehouse routed to municipal drainage in accordance with the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not mandatory for office-based e-commerce. If a distribution warehouse is occupied, obtain a Fire Safety Certificate of Compliance from the Samoa National Fire and Emergency Services Authority, a structural occupancy clearance for the premises, and comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2011 for workplace conditions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Ministry of Finance, Apia; operating the SRA Taxpayer Central Accounting System (TCAS) e-filing portal and the ASYCUDA World customs clearance platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity incorporating as an International Company files through a licensed registered agent with the Samoa International Companies Registrar within the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour. Upon issue of the Certificate of Incorporation under the International Companies Act 1987, the registered agent submits an SRA Taxpayer Registration application (prescribed T1 form in TCAS) attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Association, registered agent consent, director and shareholder identification documents, and evidence of the registered office in Samoa. The SRA issues a Tax Identification Number (TIN) to the International Company, which is required for payment of the annual government fee and for any limited administrative filings. A separate VAGST registration is required only when the International Company makes taxable supplies in or into Samoa; an International Company whose operations are exclusively offshore mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery settlement is not obligated to register for VAGST. The TIN is also practically required to enable the repatriation of foreign exchange through a Samoan commercial bank and to substantiate the 20-year tax exemption certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no check-the-box, fiscal unity, or hybrid mismatch election in its tax code. The International Company may elect under s.85 of the International Companies Act 1987 to domesticate or convert into a local company, thereby revoking its tax-exempt-zone status and subjecting future worldwide income to the standard Samoan corporate income tax rate of 27%. Without such election, the entity remains a non-resident, tax-exempt International Company. For VAGST purposes, a registrable International Company may elect a one-month, two-month, or six-month taxable cycle and may apply to the Commissioner for approval to use the cash (payments) accounting basis rather than the standard invoice basis.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992 (as consolidated and amended), administered by the Samoa Revenue Authority.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 in taxable turnover within any 12-month period (GST Act 1992, s.10). Where an International Company's supplies are exclusively exported goods and offshore COD retail services, the entity is not required to register for VAGST because such supplies are zero-rated or outside the scope of Samoan tax. Non-resident suppliers of remote or digital services to consumers located in Samoa may be subject to separate offshore supplier VAGST registration rules, but those rules do not capture physical goods delivered outside Samoa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping mandate is currently in force in Samoa. VAGST tax invoices must contain the prescribed particulars under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992, including supplier name and TIN, buyer name, description of supply, date, tax-exclusive consideration, and VAGST amount. Export consignments are cleared electronically through the ASYCUDA World customs system, requiring lodgment of an export declaration (CusEx) subject to risk-based inspection. No SRA API or digital stamping obligation is imposed on an International Company's invoices issued to overseas COD customers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated where the goods are supplied to a non-resident, are physically exported from Samoa, and documentary proof of export is retained. Services directly in connection with exported goods, including freight, insurance, and logistics, are likewise zero-rated. The International Company must not take delivery or make local supply in Samoa; title to the goods must pass outside Samoa for the zero-rating to apply. A VAGST refund may be claimed only by a registered International Company carrying excess input credits; an unregistered International Company does not charge Samoan VAGST on its foreign COD sales and therefore has no local refund entitlement. Breach of the International Companies Act operational restrictions, such as carrying on local business within Samoa, would jeopardize the 20-year tax exemption and the zero-rating position.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CusEx) accepted by Samoa Customs through ASYCUDA World
Original Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Commercial invoice and packing list for the COD consignment
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 from the receiving Samoan bank, or Airwallex settlement statement
COD settlement reconciliation report issued by the local logistics remittance agent
Certificate of Insurance or cargo insurance certificate, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Samoa Revenue Authority may audit zero-rated export claims for up to five years from the end of the relevant taxable period. Where export documentation is defective or goods are not physically exported, zero-rating is reversed, VAGST is assessed at the standard 15% rate, and any refunded input credits are clawed back with interest. The Tax Administration Act 2015 applies tiered shortfall penalties scaled by culpability, ranging from failure to take reasonable care up to intentional disregard, in addition to overdue-tax interest. The Goods and Services Tax Act 1992 separately criminalizes false or misleading export claims with monetary fines and imprisonment. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days exposes the International Company to Central Bank of Samoa exchange-control penalties, suspension of the exporter's ASYCUDA clearance facility, and refusal of future zero-rating declarations. Given the COD payment rails of Airwallex and local logistics remittance, coordinated anti-money-laundering scrutiny may apply to settlement flows, with potential referral to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) acting as the sole monetary authority and exchange control administrator under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984; the CBS approves all foreign exchange transactions through licensed commercial banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tālā (WST) is classified as a managed-float currency with controlled convertibility. Current account transactions are broadly free from restriction, but all payments to non-residents require authorised dealer approval, supporting invoices, and a designated foreign exchange purpose code. Capital account transactions, including inbound foreign direct investment, loans, guarantees, and outward remittances of profit or capital, are subject to CBS licensing or notification, with repatriation of proceeds from an International Company generally permitted only after a tax/exempt status declaration. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders of an International Company is allowed under the International Companies Act 1987 but must be routed through a licensed Samoan bank and supported by audited financial statements or a certified solvency/round-trip declaration. Hidden hurdles include a 0.5% foreign exchange levy on certain outward remittances and a historical suspicion of capital flight that triggers enhanced documentary review for transfers to high-risk jurisdictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa imposes a general exchange control obligation requiring all export proceeds to be repatriated to Samoa within 180 days of shipment. However, an International Company (IC) that qualifies as a non-resident controlled offshore entity under the International Companies Act 1987 is normally exempted from the mandatory conversion to WST, provided the proceeds are maintained in a foreign-currency account designated as an IC Foreign Currency Account. For resident trading entities, the mandatory surrender ratio is 0% (full retention of hard currency in an approved foreign-currency account), but the exporter must provide the CBS with quarterly proof of receipt. If the IC engages in any domestic retail or cash-on-delivery collection activity within Samoa, the exchange control treatment deems those collections as domestic income, requiring conversion to WST and standard surrender/commercial banking compliance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a primary local bank account, Medium as a supplementary collection/disbursement rail. Samoa does not license or regulate offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Wise, Revolut) as banks; they cannot hold WST client funds or issue local IBANs. However, an IC with a foreign-currency account at an authorised dealer can use EMI platforms for inbound cash flows from emerging-market COD customers and for outbound logistics payments only if the EMI is the correspondent/collector of a Samoan bank or operates under a reciprocal arrangement. Legal constraints include the CBS prohibition on unlicensed cross-border money service businesses, the anti-money-laundering requirement that all value transfers must pass through a licensed bank, and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit’s requirement to report any non-bank payment intermediary exceeding WST 20,000. Recommended structure: use the local bank account as the principal clearing node and the EMI as a virtual sub-account for low-value COD receipts in soft currencies.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not required to appear physically if the account is opened through a licensed Samoan bank’s remote onboarding desk, provided that the bank performs video identification, cryptographic proof of identity, and notarisation of passport and corporate documents by a recognised notary. However, in practice, at least one executive director or the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) must attend a virtual interview with the bank’s compliance officer; physical presence is mandated only when the bank detects red flags such as PEP status, high-risk jurisdiction linkage, or inability to source documentary proof of business. For an International Company, the registered agent (usually a licensed Samoan trustee/management company) must certify the board resolution and sign the account opening mandate in person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Samoa International Company with nominal bearer-share history or ambiguity in the Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) ledger
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the International Company’s certificate of incorporation; current register of directors and shareholders issued by the registered agent; a formal UBO declaration under the Companies (Amendment) Act 2018; organisational chart showing 100% chain of ownership; sworn statement that no bearer shares exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-on-delivery (COD) business model with high-volume small-value cash payments from emerging-market consumers, causing unexplained cash deposits in the operational account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed e-commerce logistics and settlement-flow narrative; signed contracts with logistics partners (e.g., local courier aggregators); copies of daily cash-out settlement reports; sampled customer invoices and payment confirmations; treasury policy requiring direct settlement to the bank account from the courier’s escrow account rather than cash deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions involving high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions through the emerging-market network (e.g., OFAC, EU, or Samoa sanctions-list screening hits)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standard AML policy with jurisdiction-specific risk matrix; geolocation and IP-log evidence proving that the beneficial owner and order processes are located in clean jurisdictions; third-party screening results from a reputable compliance vendor; enhanced due diligence (EDD) reports for every counterparty in high-risk countries; a commitment to onboard all financial flow through the Samoan licensed bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate foreign exchange conversion and remittance activity inconsistent with the declared business purpose (mail-order retail with COD)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or management-prepared financial statements for the IC; bank statement reconciliation report; inventory and logistics flow documents; customer side agreements; licensing certificates for export/import; a cross-border funds-flow diagram matching each remittance to a specific trade invoice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company tax-exempt status used to mask a de facto domestic Samoan trading operation, which triggers local VAT and income tax liability
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Letter from the Samoan Ministry for Revenue confirming the IC’s offshore-exempt status; certification from the Registered Agent that no Samoan-sourced sales occur; evidence that the distribution hub is outside Samoa; a compliance undertaking to re-classify the entity as a resident company if any domestic COD activity begins.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital contributions to the International Company’s Samoan bank account must be routed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 messages with a clear funds-purpose narrative. The approved routing is: (1) foreign shareholder sends funds to the IC’s foreign-currency account at a licensed Samoan bank, using purpose code 'C1' (Capital Investment) or 'F1' (Foreign Direct Investment) as defined by CBS exchange-control circulars; (2) the bank verifies the source-of-funds document (shareholder resolution, subscription agreement, bank statement) and the IC’s certificate of good standing; (3) if the capital is in a currency other than WST, the bank will require a conversion order only if the IC wishes to hold Samoan tālā; otherwise the amount is retained in the original currency in a designated IC foreign-currency account. For capital above WST 500,000, a prior CBS General Permission application must be filed with a certified board resolution and a subscribed capital statement. No inward funds may be received in cash; all injections must be authenticated by an electronic SWIFT message or a certified correspondent bank instruction. The bank will issue a 'Certificate of Inward Remittance' to the IC for future foreign-exchange hedging and repatriation purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements to offshore suppliers, logistics carriers, and telecommunication/COD platforms, the IC may use three clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 for direct bank-to-bank payments exceeding USD 10,000, requiring an invoice, customs declaration, and a CBS export/import purpose code (e.g., code M2 for general imports, code C2 for trade payments); (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) at sight or usance for high-value purchases, issued via ANZ or BSP with the underlying sales contract and airway bill; (c) local payment platforms connected to the corresponding EMTL provider (e.g., Airwallex, local logistics remittance solutions) for low-value recurring COD disbursements, but every aggregated settlement must be reported to the bank monthly. Outbound remittances below WST 20,000 may be executed under a bank’s delegated authority; above that threshold, a CBS exchange-control form must be completed. The disbursement corridor to Samoa’s emerging-market target countries (e.g., Pacific Island states, Southeast Asia, or African COD markets) must be pre-approved by the bank’s AML unit, and the bank will require a trip-wire code 'T1' if the beneficiary is a high-risk jurisdiction. Standby L/Cs may be used to guarantee logistics escrow accounts, but the IC must hold identical collateral or a cash margin at the issuing bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts with authorised Samoan banks up to 12 months tenors, backed by a declaration of underlying commercial exposure (e.g., USD/WST, AUD/WST, SGD/WST).

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for non-WST currency pairs quoted by offshore banks, such as USD/CNY or USD/EUR, because the WST is not a deliverable offshore currency; the Samoan bank may act as a pass-through arranger under a CBS notification.

Cross-currency swaps involving WST and a major convertible currency are permissible for a licensed Samoan bank counterparty, but only with a documented trade or capital-flow obligation and CBS approval for tenors exceeding 12 months.
Vanilla FX options (call/put on WST) may be permitted for hedging of confirmed trade receivables, but only where the bank obtains a copy of the underlying receivable and the option is booked onshore.
Interest-rate/FX combination swaps are generally not available to non-resident ICs; a more efficient hedging vehicle is parallel lending via the Samoan bank's international branch network.

In-kind hedging through multi-currency accounts (holding USD, AUD, EUR, NZD, CNY) is expressly permitted as an internal treasury operation, but the CBS must receive quarterly returns of the aggregate open position.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company annual government renewal fee (authorization to continue in force)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation; fee must be remitted before the renewal date, with a customary 30-day grace period from the anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late remittance attracts a monetary surcharge imposed by the Registrar; continued non-payment after formal notice leads to administrative strike-off, loss of legal personality, and inability to enforce contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered agent annual attesting that the registered office, resident agent, directors, members, and beneficial ownership records are compliant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal date, coinciding with the government fee anniversary cycle; filing accepted on or before the renewal date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default constitutes a statutory offense by the registered agent; unresolved non-compliance triggers a Registrar compliance notice and eventual strike-off under the International Companies Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is compulsory for a Samoa International Company irrespective of revenue, assets, or shareholder count; an audit arises only if the articles of incorporation or a shareholder special resolution expressly require it
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No local GAAP or IFRS filing mandate is imposed on International Companies; accounting records may be maintained on any consistent accounting basis, with IFRS accepted as the benchmark standard if a voluntary audit is commissioned

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Samoa International Companies are not subject to a statutory UBO filing; however, the registered agent must annually confirm that its customer due diligence and beneficial ownership records remain current, and the company must notify the agent within 14 days of any share transfer or change in control
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registered Agent and Registered Office Records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable as a compulsory matter; voluntary certified audit typically USD 2,500 - USD 6,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for qualifying International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987; standard domestic corporate rate is 25% for non-IC entities
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are exempt from all income tax, stamp duty, and exchange control regulations; no statutory tax holidays are required; a one-time annual license fee applies

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (ICAR) and Tax Identification Number (TIN) registration via the Samoa Ministry for Revenue (MFR) electronic portal; no corporate income tax return is required for tax-exempt ICs
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days of the anniversary of the company's incorporation date for the Annual Return; any economic substance or beneficial ownership declaration is due within the same window

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name as registered with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
Use the registered agent's address; no physical presence is required
Provide full names, residential addresses, and passport numbers for all officers

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder register and beneficial owner declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose ultimate beneficial owners; maintain strict AML/KYC records for the cash-on-delivery e-commerce model

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of no local taxable activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that no domestic-source income is derived from Samoa; treaty protection under the DTA with China may apply

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of WST 500 for the Annual Return, plus WST 50 per day for continued default; failure to file may result in deregistration and director disqualification under the International Companies Act 1987

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for International Companies distributing dividends to non-residents; domestic companies face a final withholding tax rate of 15%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Samoa Ministry for Revenue, complete the relevant WHT declaration on the MFR portal, and submit the TRC alongside the dividend distribution documentation; the Samoa-China DTA limits dividend WHT to 5% for shareholdings of 25% or greater and 10% in all other cases
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalty or interest paid by a domestic entity is 15%; under the Samoa-China DTA, royalties are capped at 10%, and interest at 10%; interest derived by a financial enterprise may qualify for a 0% rate under the DTA, subject to beneficial ownership certification

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa does not maintain mandatory Local File or Master File rules for International Companies; however, transactions above WST 200,000 in a fiscal year require contemporaneous documentation for DTA and substance purposes
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2021 requires an International Company with relevant banking, distribution, or intellectual property activities to maintain economic substance in Samoa, including adequate physical presence, qualified employees, and core income-generating activities in Samoa; a mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery settlement must file an annual Economic Substance Statement and assess the presence of distribution services revenue

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally filing a false Economic Substance Declaration or failing to declare beneficial ownership to conceal the geographic location of cash-on-delivery settlement activities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A fine up to SAT 500,000 and a period of imprisonment not exceeding three years under the Tax Administration Act 2004
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax and fines; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed pending investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the International Company as a pure pass-through for online COD retail without any board control or substance in Samoa, used solely to avoid source-state tax on foreign e-commerce profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Deregistration of the International Company, immediate revocation of tax-exempt status, and a retrospective levy of the 25% domestic corporate income tax on accumulated profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal restitution orders for the underpaid tax and may be disqualified from holding offshore directorships for up to ten years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling cash-on-delivery proceeds through remittance rails without enforceable customer due diligence, anti-money laundering policies, or suspicious transaction reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty up to SAT 500,000 per breach under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2018, plus forfeiture of any unattributed funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or compliance officers demonstrating gross negligence are personally liable for the penalty amount, with a potential custodial sentence of up to 12 months
